task.prompt: Write the stored procedure sp(arg1 VARCHAR2, arg2 NUMBER, arg3 VARCHAR2, arg4 VARCHAR2), exactly as required by the attached design document. In business terms, it should set the percentage budgeted on budget rows that match the first argument and meet the document's conditions, and set the location on school rows that match the third argument and meet its conditions. The first argument is the budget-invested percentage to match against on budget rows; the second is the new percentage budgeted for those rows; the third is the mascot to match against on school rows; the fourth is the new location for those rows. The attached design document is the full set of requirements, including all thresholds, text values, and error handling. Return only the complete stored procedure.

materials.text:
## 1. Overview
The sp procedure is an Oracle PL/SQL stored procedure with exactly four arguments. It updates budget percentage and school location when the usual checks pass, keeps one updated-row count across both parts, and uses `sp_savepoint`.

## 2. Interface

| Position | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | VARCHAR2 | The exact budget-invested percentage text that makes a budget row eligible for the budget update. |
| 2 | NUMBER | The new percentage budgeted assigned to eligible budget rows. |
| 3 | VARCHAR2 | The exact mascot text that makes a school row eligible for the school update. |
| 4 | VARCHAR2 | The new location assigned to eligible school rows. |

## 3. Data
Uses the budget records and the school records: the budget-invested/budgeted fields and amount on one side, mascot/enrollment/location on the other.

## 4. Rule catalogue
Text matches are exact. If the mascot side has no match for the third argument, raise application error -20002 with the exact message `No School record matches the mascot; budget updates skipped`. If the combined work changes nothing, raise application error -20001 with the exact message `No matching records were updated`.

## 5. Processing specification
Create `sp_savepoint` first, check the mascot side early, and use the overall budgeted-amount and enrollment averages for the two passes. Do the budget pass before the school pass: set qualifying budget percentages to the second argument, then set qualifying school locations to the fourth. Count each qualifying update, including the already-same-value kind.

## 6. Edge cases and error behaviour
After the savepoint, every exception rolls back to `sp_savepoint` and re-raises the original exception. A successful finish issues no COMMIT; the caller deals with the transaction. That’s it.
